messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT ALERT — p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate (hosted-api-prod)
incident-bot: summary: p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s starting ~5m ago. Alerting threshold: 1200ms. Affected route: streaming & non-streaming. Link: https://grafana.redwood/services/p95-p99-latency?panel=serve
maria_oncall: on it. escalating to SRE + runtime. Paging @sam_sre @dave_runtime. Any initial notes on change windows? :eyes:
sam_sre: I see a correlated drop in healthy replicas on the serving autoscaler around the same time. CPU on the scheduling plane looks normal, but there are lots of connection resets to backend GPUs.
dave_runtime: pulling logs for model-serving-pool-3. Also checking kv cache errors. Give me a minute.
olivia_prod: customer reports: a few streaming sessions stalled and client retries spiked. Started ~10:22 UTC. Looks like p95 doubled and p99 spiked higher.
priya_support: triaging incoming customer tickets, marking impacted apps (dynamic-chat, embeddings-batch). Notifying sales for top-tier customers.
maria_oncall: quick triage checklist (run these):
1) check autoscaler & pool health
2) query p99 per-region per-model
3) see if fallback routing triggered
4) check kernel OOM / dmesg on nodes
5) toggle streaming->non-streaming for a sample customer
Use runbook: /runbooks/latency-regression
sam_sre: ran the health checks — autoscaler tried to scale up but pods are stuck in ContainerCreating with `MountVolume.WaitForAttach` delays. Node attach times jumped.
dave_runtime: kv cache logs show a flurry of throttling for prefix-cache writes: `KVCacheWriteError: EBUSY` across several instances. Could be a shared disk or NFS issue. Also seeing repeated gRPC stream resets: `RST_STREAM code:2`.
olivia_prod: Grafana panel: p99 per shard shows one shard (shard-7) behind the others and correlates with higher IO wait. Screenshot posted in thread.
maria_oncall: runbook step: test a simple health endpoint on a problematic pod. dave, can you paste curl output from one of the stuck pods?
dave_runtime: executing:

```
kubectl exec -n serving model-srv-7 -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
```

stdout: `{"ok":false,"details":"KV cache init timeout, disk I/O high"}`
sam_sre: checking node-level iostat:

```
iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 0.30 120.00 1000.00 48000.00 400.00 12.34 35.12 1.23 36.78 0.90 93.2
```

sam_sre: %util ~93% on NVME, high avg queue; that would explain attach/latency issues.
maria_oncall: probable hypothesis: transient storage IO saturation on a subset of nodes causing KV cache writes to fail -> increased queuing -> request timeouts / stream stalls. Immediate mitigations?
dave_runtime: short-term mitigations:
- cordon + drain affected nodes (shard-7) and let pods re-schedule to healthier nodes
- enable fallback routing for requests currently pinned to shard-7
- disable streaming chunked responses for impacted customers (reduce open streams)

I can run drain on the 3 affected nodes. Need approval.
maria_oncall: approve drain + fallback routing. Prioritize top-tier customers by maintaining non-streamed responses.
priya_support: preparing templated customer message: "We are experiencing elevated latencies for streaming endpoints. We're actively mitigating and will update in 30m."
sam_sre: initiating cordon/drain:

```
kubectl cordon node-az3-nvme07
kubectl drain node-az3-nvme07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

sam_sre: pods are rescheduling; new pods on nodes with lower IO. Observed p95 trending down on those pods.
dave_runtime: enabling routing fallback in gateway policy for shard-7:

```
PATCH /gateway/routes/fallback
{ "source_shard": "shard-7", "fallback_model": "redwood-small-v2", "streaming": false }
```

Result: about 30% of requests for shard-7 now routed to fallback model. Should buy time while nodes recover.
olivia_prod: metrics update: p95 global is back to ~300ms from 600ms, p99 still around 1.1s but coming down. Streaming stalls reduced by retry logic.
maria_oncall: good. continue to watch for 30m. open incident ticket and assign owner for postmortem. Who's taking incident lead?
dave_runtime: I can own the postmortem. Will gather logs and timelines.
priya_support: customer comms scheduled every 30m. First update sent. :white_check_mark:
sam_sre: follow-up: NVME firmware on those nodes had an older driver; opened infra ticket to investigate IO patterns and possible hardware replacement. Marking as follow-up for engineering-ops.
maria_oncall: recording next action items: 
- dave: collect KV cache traces + pod logs (owner) 
- sam: node-level iostat + cloud provider attach logs (owner) 
- priya: collect affected customer list & message history
- olivia: verify streaming fallback didn't introduce quality regression on redwood-small
- me(maria): coordinate postmortem and link to incident channel

Please add any additional notes here.
dave_runtime: attaching sample logs snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:22:13Z model-srv-7 ERROR KVCacheWriteError: EBUSY path=/var/lib/kvcache/keys shard=7
2026-03-15T10:22:14Z model-srv-7 WARN stream reset id=0x1f code=2 peer=10.10.7.21
```

Also I confirmed that after reschedule, new pod health: `{"ok":true}`.
maria_oncall: timeline capture: alert fired 10:22, cordon/drain 10:28-10:32, fallback routing enabled 10:30, p95 improvement visible 10:34, p99 improving by 10:40. Plan: keep incident open for 2 hours or until p99 stable <900ms for 30min.
priya_support: logging customer tickets and tagging severity. Sending update now.
olivia_prod: noticed one noisy customer with heavy long-lived streaming sessions. Suggest a follow-up quota/connection limit for streaming per-tenant to reduce single-tenant tail impact.
sam_sre: noted. creating infra follow-up ticket for connection limits + NVMe health checks.
maria_oncall: great work team. leaving the channel to follow handoff procedures — @dave_runtime will be incident lead. Incident will stay in this thread; please post updates here. Ending on-call note: escalate to platform-eng if we see recurrence within 24h. :lock:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, p95 improved. Incident owner: dave_runtime. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
